title: Discreteness and local quasi-finiteness over a field
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], together with a morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ of algebraic spaces over $S$ (for instance $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$); all fibre products below are over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Give $|X|$ its atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Suppose $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type, tested on representable etale scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Say that this map is locally quasi-finite if every representable etale scheme chart $U\to X$ has locally quasi-finite composite $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ in the scheme sense [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Then $|X|$ is discrete (every singleton is open) if and only if $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally quasi-finite. If in addition $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated, meaning that its diagonal is representable and is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion], then finiteness of $|X|$ implies that $|X|$ is discrete. No quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed. The empty space is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0ACA (lemma-conditions-on-space-over-field), conditions (2) and (5), and (1) implies (2) for decent spaces; Tag 088J (lemma-locally-separated-decent) applies to a separated algebraic space.

proof.text: Regard $X$ as its discrete fibred groupoid. Its representable diagonal and etale scheme atlas make it Deligne--Mumford: the diagonal is in particular representable by algebraic spaces, and descent of objects is exactly the sheaf condition. The ordinary and stack local finite-type notions agree on algebraic spaces by [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus]. The point topology agrees as well by [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. Thus, if $|X|$ is discrete, [lem-sfb-dm-field-etale-chart-quasifinite] applies to $X/k$ and gives local quasi-finiteness of every representable etale scheme chart over $k$, precisely the required definition.

source.place: Tag 0ACA (lemma-conditions-on-space-over-field), proof of (2) iff (5) and the finite-point decent case; using the existing DM-chart specialization and the stronger quasi-separated chart bound.

proof.text: Conversely, assume chartwise local quasi-finiteness and choose a point-surjective etale scheme atlas $p:U\to X$ by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. For $u\in U$, its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type by hypothesis and quasi-finite at $u$ by [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated]: $\{u\}$ is open in the inverse image of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, namely all of $U$. The point map of $p$ is open, so $\{p(u)\}=|p|(\{u\})$ is open in $|X|$. Surjectivity proves discreteness.

source.place: Tag 0ACA (lemma-conditions-on-space-over-field), proof of (2) iff (5) and the finite-point decent case; using the existing DM-chart specialization and the stronger quasi-separated chart bound.

proof.text: Now assume separatedness over $k$ and finiteness of $|X|$. Its absolute diagonal factors as $X\to X\times_kX\to X\times_{\mathbf Z}X$. The first arrow is a closed immersion on scheme tests by hypothesis. The second is the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}(k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}k)$ induced by multiplication, which is surjective since $a$ is the image of $a\otimes1$. It is a closed immersion by the affine quotient characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion]; the product identification is [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Base change and composition preserve closed immersions on the scheme tests by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]. On affine tests their inverse images are spectra of quotient rings, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact]. This verifies the absolute quasi-separatedness hypothesis for [lem-sfb-space-qc-etale-fibre-bound].

source.place: Tag 0ACA (lemma-conditions-on-space-over-field), proof of (2) iff (5) and the finite-point decent case; using the existing DM-chart specialization and the stronger quasi-separated chart bound.

proof.text: Fix a representable etale chart $a:V\to X$ with $V$ affine. It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], so [lem-sfb-space-qc-etale-fibre-bound] supplies finite geometric fibres. For $x\in|X|$, choose a field-valued representative and extend its field to an algebraic closure using [def-weil-algebraic-closure], obtaining $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$. The surjectivity of the cartesian point map in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] shows that $|V\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega|\to |a|^{-1}(\{x\})$ is onto: pair each $v$ above $x$ with the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Thus this point fibre is finite. Since $|X|$ is finite, $|V|$ is the finite union of these finite fibres and is finite.

source.place: Tag 0ACA (lemma-conditions-on-space-over-field), proof of (2) iff (5) and the finite-point decent case; using the existing DM-chart specialization and the stronger quasi-separated chart bound.

proof.text: The composite $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type by the chart hypothesis and has finite point fibre $|V|$. Apply [pqf-lem-locqf-fibre-discrete]; its conclusion makes the scheme fibre discrete. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] its first projection is a homeomorphism onto all of $V$, so $|V|$ is discrete. For any $x\in|X|$, [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] gives such an affine chart and a point $v$ above $x$ (use the affine component containing a preimage in its disjoint affine atlas). That component $V_i\subseteq W$ is open, so for every scheme $T\to X$ the scheme $T\times_XV_i$ is an open subscheme of $T\times_XW$; it is etale over $T$ because local finite presentation, flatness and unramifiedness in [def-weil-etale-morphism] are local on the source. Thus $V_i\to X$ is a representable etale chart with $V_i$ affine, to which the argument above applies with $V=V_i$. Since its point map is open, $\{x\}=|a|(\{v\})$ is open. This proves the final assertion. For $X=\varnothing$ both the chart condition and the singleton condition are vacuous; none of the arguments require a finite atlas or quasi-compactness of $X$.
